title: Multiple Distance Ramsey Bounds For Graphs in Euclidean Spaces
summary: For a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ and a finite graph $H$, let $χ_H(\mathbb{R}^n;A)$ be the minimum number of colors required to color $\mathbb{R}^n$ while avoiding a monochromatic copy of $H$ whose edges have distances in $A$. Extending the graph-copy framework of Axenovich, Liu, and Sagdeev and a multiple distance theorem of Naslund, we prove for any positive integer $m$, \[χ_H(\mathbb{R}^n;m):=\max_{\substack{A \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{>0} \\ |A|=m}} χ_H(\mathbb{R}^n;A) \geq \left(Γ_χ\sqrt{\frac{m+1}{Ξ(H)}}+o(1)\right)^n.\] Here, $Γ_χ$ is a constant and $Ξ(H)$ is an explicit…
